title: Build the microjson strict RFC 8259 parser and serializer from its sealed spec
goal: Implement the microjson codec exactly as written in assets/gc-404/SPEC.md, from scratch, at workspace/gc-404/microjson.py, without touching Python's json module (the sealed suite scans the source and fails on it). The spec's deliberately tricky sections cover 1-based line/col error positions, UTF-16 surrogate-pair decoding with lone-surrogate rejection, the strict number grammar, and bool-before-int serialization order. This is a multi-session build: plan the lexer/parser structure, implement loads and dumps incrementally, run the sealed suite repeatedly, and drive every failure back to a spec clause until all tests pass.
process_expectations: A plan artifact workspace/gc-404/plan.md exists before implementation, decomposing the codec into lexing, value parsing, error positioning, and serialization milestones with a verification step per milestone.
workspace/gc-404/runs.log shows the sealed suite executed after each milestone, with summary lines; at least one RED run precedes the final GREEN.
Every intermediate failing test node id is logged with the RFC/spec clause it traced to and the fix; counts alone are insufficient.
Honest cost logging in workspace/gc-404/cost.json (spend per milestone, cumulative).
Recovery after RED is documented as diagnosis -> fix -> re-run; assets/gc-404/test_accept.py is never edited and the json module is never imported.
